l1.summary: A tool that reads any software project's source code and produces a structured summary of what the software does, organized by reading priority. It then checks whether descriptions of the software (written by others) are accurate, complete, and free of jargon — catching made-up claims and ensuring every description traces back to real code.

features.label: Automatic code structure reading
features.description: Reads all source files in a software project and identifies the building blocks: what functions exist, what classes exist, how they relate to each other, and what documentation the developers wrote about them
features.trigger_description: When a user points the tool at a software project folder
features.confidence_reason: Clear from file_discovery (enumerates files), node_builder (extracts functions/classes), edge_builder (finds relationships), and ast_extractor (orchestrates all three). Docstrings explicitly describe this purpose.

features.label: Smart reading order assignment
features.description: Analyzes which parts of the code are most important (most referenced by other parts, or serve as main entry points) and assigns a priority reading order so that the most critical pieces are understood first
features.trigger_description: Runs automatically after code structure reading completes
features.confidence_reason: TopologyAnalyzer orchestrates graph building, entry point detection, and batch assignment. Docstrings and method names clearly indicate priority-based ordering.

features.label: Description accuracy checking
features.description: Takes a written description of what the software does and checks it for five types of problems: wrong format, missing pieces, use of technical jargon, made-up claims about code that doesn't exist, and invented relationships between features
features.trigger_description: When a user submits a description to be verified against the code structure
features.confidence_reason: OutputValidator runs exactly 5 named checks (schema, coverage, language, anchor, relation). Each check class has a clear single responsibility with descriptive docstrings.

features.label: Command-line operation
features.description: Provides three commands that users can run from a terminal: one to read code structure, one to verify descriptions, and one to start a connection point for other tools
features.trigger_description: When a user types a command in their terminal
features.confidence_reason: Three distinct command files (extract_cmd, validate_cmd, mcp_serve_cmd) registered in main.py. Click decorators and docstrings clearly describe each command's purpose.

features.label: Integration with other AI tools
features.description: Allows any compatible AI tool to use the code reading and description verification capabilities without custom setup, by exposing them as standardized tool calls
features.trigger_description: Starts when the connection point is launched, then responds to requests from connected tools
features.confidence_reason: TheDoorMCPServer class registers two tools (extract_structure, validate_output) with clear input schemas. The server uses stdio transport for local communication.

feature_relations.relation: After code structure is read, the priority ordering automatically runs on the results to determine what should be understood first
feature_relations.inferred_reason: Both are orchestrated sequentially by the CLI extract command and MCP extract_structure tool. No direct call edge exists between extraction and topology modules — they are composed at the command layer.

feature_relations.relation: The code structure reading results are used as the ground truth when checking whether descriptions are accurate
feature_relations.inferred_reason: OutputValidator.validate() accepts structure_json as input, which is the output of extraction + topology. The CLI validate command requires both files. No direct call edge exists because they run as separate user commands.

feature_relations.relation: The extract command triggers the code reading process
The validate command triggers the description checking process
